flags.water-sewer: Whether the parcel has access to water and sewer service is currently unknown and hasn't been checked or scored [utilities.water_sewer]. You should ask the water authority to confirm availability before relying on this [utilities.water_sewer].
flags.adu: A proposed rule (not yet law) would allow up to 2 accessory dwelling units by right, with size and height limits, but this depends on Bill 2025-1545 which is still being considered by Council [zoning.district, reform.status]. Since it is only proposed, it cannot be counted on yet [reform.status].
flags.parking-minimum: The same proposed, not-yet-law bill would remove the requirement to build off-street parking, potentially freeing up land and money for housing instead [reform.status]. This is still under Council review and not in effect [reform.status].
flags.affordable-housing-bonus: The proposed bill also includes an optional bonus for adding affordable housing, available since this parcel is not in the existing Inclusionary Housing Overlay [overlay.iz, reform.status]. This bonus is not law yet and depends on the bill passing [reform.status].
flags.gap-financing: This parcel is in a neighborhood with low assessed land values, which often means projects need extra funding help (called 'gap financing') to become financially workable [hood.median_land_psf]. This is just a note, not a penalty against the parcel [hood.median_land_psf].
flags.phfa-infill: Because this is a vacant lot in a low-value area, it may qualify for special infill or blight-related scoring under state housing finance agency (PHFA) programs [landuse.vacant, hood.median_land_psf]. You should check this against PHFA's current criteria before assuming eligibility [hood.median_land_psf].
flags.public-owner: The parcel is owned by the City, which may make it easier to acquire through the City's public property disposition process, though this is not guaranteed [owner.type]. Anyone interested should confirm the exact process directly with the City [owner.type].
